title: UFO Sightings and Political Alignment in the U.S.
text:
This project analyzes UFO sighting records from the National UFO Reporting Center to study whether state political alignment is associated with differences in sighting frequency.
Early results show:

Democratic-leaning states tend to report higher average sightings.

Mann–Whitney, chi-square, and Poisson regression all support this pattern.

Narrative descriptions and sighting characteristics (shape, duration) appear similar across political groups.

Upcoming work includes adjusting for population, incorporating additional state-level covariates, and expanding the text analysis of witness narratives.

title: Alcohol, Music, Gender, and Oxytocin
text:
This project uses a 3×2×2 factorial design to test the effects of alcohol type, music genre, and gender on blood oxytocin levels. We fit a three-way ANOVA and check all model assumptions.

Gender explains ~99% of the variance in oxytocin response.
Alcohol type and music genre show no meaningful main or interaction effects.

title: Panel Analysis of U.S. Cigarette Consumption
text:
Using the Cigar dataset, this project models per-capita cigarette sales across 46 states from 1963–1992.
We compare:

Pooled OLS
Fixed effects
Random effects

The Hausman test and F-tests support the fixed effects model, which we use to estimate price elasticity and discuss taxation policy implications.

title: About Me
text:
I’m an undergraduate at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), double majoring in Statistics & Data Science and Economics (graduating June 2026). I work at the intersection of analytics, technology, and business — building things that turn messy data into clear decisions.
My academic work spans statistical modeling, machine learning, and applied econometrics, with a strong focus on how data products are actually built, deployed, and used. Whether it’s a predictive model, an analytics dashboard, or a generative-AI tool, I care about making the output useful, not just technically correct.

title: About Me

Core Interests
Predictive modeling and ML, experimental design and causal inference, business intelligence and data visualization, AI applications in finance and customer analytics, and using statistical thinking to solve interdisciplinary problems.

These roles have sharpened my communication, project management, and ability to work across diverse teams.

title: AI Chatbot for Investment Education
text:
Overview
This project builds a multi-agent, LLM-powered chatbot for client-facing financial education on an investment platform. The goal is to let retail clients ask natural-language questions about investing concepts and get accurate, compliant responses — without replacing human advisors.

title: AI Chatbot for Investment Education
text:
Architecture
The system uses a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline:

Document store — a curated knowledge base of investment education content (prospectuses, FAQs, regulatory disclosures) embedded with OpenAI embeddings and indexed in a vector database
Retriever — semantic search over the knowledge base to ground each response in source material
LLM layer — GPT-4 generates responses strictly from retrieved context, avoiding hallucinated financial advice
Compliance guardrails — prompt-level and output-level filters to flag or block responses that stray into personalized investment advice
